props.gloss_en: one who enters to visit the sick says: 'it is Shabbat, [one refrains] from crying out, and healing is near to come'
R' Meir: [he says] 'it (Shabbat) is able to have compassion'
R' Yehuda: [he says] 'may the Omnipresent have compassion on you and on the sick of Israel'
R' Yose: [he says] 'may the Omnipresent have compassion on you among the sick of Israel'
Shevna of Jerusalem, on entering, would say 'shalom'
and on leaving he would say: 'it is Shabbat, [one refrains] from crying out, and healing is near to come; His compassion is great; and rest in peace'
R' Chanina: one who has a sick person in his house must include him among the sick of Israel
whose view does R' Chanina's dictum follow? R' Yose's
R' Chanina: with difficulty they permitted comforting mourners on Shabbat
R' Chanina: with difficulty they permitted visiting the sick on Shabbat
Rabba bar bar Chana: sometimes R' Elazar said 'may the Omnipresent remember you for peace'
and sometimes he said to him [in Aramaic] 'may the Merciful One remember you for peace'
Rav Yehuda: a person should never ask for his needs in Aramaic
R' Yochanan: whoever asks for his needs in Aramaic, the ministering angels do not attend to him, for they do not recognise Aramaic
a sick person is different, for the Shechina is with him
Rav: from where that the Holy One sustains the sick? as it says 'the Lord will support him on the bed of illness' (Ps 41:4)
one who enters to visit the sick may sit neither on the bed nor on a chair, but wraps himself and sits before him
because the Shechina is above the head of the sick person
[that the Shechina is above the sick person's head] as it says 'the Lord will support him on the bed of illness'
Ravin: from where that the Holy One feeds the sick? as it says 'the Lord will support him on the bed of illness'
